names.summary: A 72-byte beacon frame with a small header, several slowly varying single-byte fields, and a number of multi-byte fields that look like float or packed data misread as integers. Evidence is weak: most fields are flat or quantised, and several correlations come from the lack of eclipse variety (every frame follows an eclipse out of view).

fields.name: status_byte_a
fields.rationale: Only 10 distinct values, median 70 in every regime, so the sun correlation comes from rare outliers. It moves with offsets 3 and 4, which suggests a state or housekeeping group. [3/3 samples agree]

fields.name: status_byte_b
fields.rationale: Median 5 in all regimes with a few large outliers. It is correlated with fields 2 and 4, so it is probably a mode or status value rather than a measurement. [3/3 samples agree]

fields.name: status_byte_c
fields.rationale: Signed byte with a constant median of -67 in every regime and sparse excursions. No physical signature is identifiable. [3/3 samples agree]

fields.name: bus_or_load_candidate
fields.rationale: The u3le value is bimodal, either near 0 or near 13.2M (about 0xC9xxxx), and higher in shadow. This looks like a misaligned float or packed field, not a real 24-bit quantity, so the power_bus hint is not trusted. [3/3 samples agree]

fields.name: shadow_linked_signed_byte
fields.rationale: Steps from about -54 in sun to 74 in shadow (rho_sun -0.73) with only 8 distinct values. It is likely a quantised sensor or part of a misaligned field; the battery hint is not credible because it shows no within-regime trend. [3/3 samples agree]

fields.name: gnss_position_eci_z
fields.rationale: Float matching ECI z position with a score of 0.97, but only 36% of frames agree with the orbit. The scale of about 992 per km is odd, so the unit is probably metres with some ambiguity. [2/3 samples agree]

fields.name: orbit_periodic_signed_value
fields.rationale: s3le with r2_orbit 0.32 and a roughly ±5M range. It repeats with orbital phase but the medians are flat across sun and shadow, so it could be a position or vector component of unknown type. [3/3 samples agree]

fields.name: orbit_periodic_u16
fields.rationale: u2le with weak orbit periodicity (r2 0.29) and values at 0 or around 17.8k to 50k. The joined carry flag suggests it is part of a larger field. [3/3 samples agree]

fields.name: bus_or_load_candidate_2
fields.rationale: u3le is bimodal, near 0 or about 12.9M, and higher in shadow, like offset 15. It is probably a misparsed float or packed value, so the power_bus hint is not trusted. [3/3 samples agree]

names.health: Not enough evidence. No counters or clocks were identified, so reboots cannot be assessed, and no field is confidently a battery or temperature. Drift values are tiny or not meaningful over 13.5 days.

names.summary: A 72-byte housekeeping beacon with a Unix timestamp, a solar-input-like field, several signed temperature-like bytes that follow sunlight, a rolling sequence counter, and a few small bytes of uncertain meaning. Every frame had an eclipse in the preceding 80 minutes, so the sun/shadow contrasts are real physics.

fields.name: unix_timestamp
fields.rationale: u4le advancing at 0.99999 s/s with Unix epoch guess and no resets. The max of 1795619439 is odd (a 2026 date), but the rate is exact. [3/3 samples agree]

fields.name: solar_panel_current
fields.rationale: u2le is exactly 0 in shadow and about 178 mean in sun (rho_sun 0.915), and it is rough. The hint is power_solar. The unit is a guess. [3/3 samples agree]

fields.name: bus_load_a
fields.rationale: Small u1 (0-21) that is higher in shadow, with r2_orbit 0.31. It moves with offset 34 but the evidence is weak. It could be a current or temperature in coarse units. [3/3 samples agree]

fields.name: bus_load_b
fields.rationale: Nearly identical to offset 33 (same profile, moves together). It is likely a paired channel such as a redundant sensor or a second current. [3/3 samples agree]

fields.name: panel_temp_1
fields.rationale: Signed byte in -10..44 that is warmer in sun (mean 17 vs 2) and falls through shadow (trend -0.57). Its profile matches the other panel temperatures. [3/3 samples agree]

fields.name: panel_temp_2
fields.rationale: Signed byte with the same sun/shadow contrast and shadow cooling trend as offset 43. It is likely another face. [3/3 samples agree]

fields.name: panel_temp_3
fields.rationale: Lagged with tau about 10 min, rho 0.655, and a cooling trend in shadow. It moves with the other signed-byte temperatures. [3/3 samples agree]

fields.name: panel_temp_4
fields.rationale: Signed byte with rho_sun 0.739, warm in sun and cooling in shadow, consistent with the panel temperature group. [3/3 samples agree]

fields.name: sequence_counter
fields.rationale: s1 that increases monotonically within passes and wraps at 8 bits (about 0.067 per second, 15 wraps). The wraps are by design, not reboots. [3/3 samples agree]

fields.name: battery_temp
fields.rationale: u1 with a narrow band (p5-p95 10-16) and a slightly warmer shadow median. The hint was power_battery, but the value is coarse and sun correlation is weak. It is probably an internal or battery temperature, and the max of 253 may be an invalid-value flag. [3/3 samples agree]

names.health: No timestamp resets are seen, and the counter wraps are expected for a one-byte sequence number. Panel temperatures swing about 15 degC between sun and shadow, which is normal. There is not enough evidence for battery health, because no clear battery voltage was identified.
